title: An Adaptive Spatial Subdivision of the Object Space for Fast Collision Detection of Animated Rigid Bodies
relevance: Primary adaptive spatial-subdivision method for animated rigid bodies; establishes prior art for adapting object-space partitions rather than fixing one uniform resolution. It does not test the present median/90th-percentile two-tier candidate-count protocol.

title: Optimized Spatial Hashing for Collision Detection of Deformable Objects
venue: Proceedings of Vision, Modeling, and Visualization 2003
relevance: Primary spatial-hashing paper. It uses a hash-compressed regular grid and empirically investigates hash function, table size, and spatial cell size for collision and self-collision detection. Its deformable tetrahedral setting differs from this AABB rigid-body benchmark.

title: Hierarchical Spatial Hashing for Real-Time Collision Detection
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Shape Modeling and Applications
relevance: Primary hierarchical spatial-hashing method that adapts grid resolution to object scale. It is the closest prior art to a multi-scale hash, but its hierarchy and application differ from a two-tier median/90th-percentile policy and must not be treated as evidence for that policy.

title: Virtual subdivision for GPU based collision detection of deformable objects using a uniform grid
relevance: Primary study of the object-size versus uniform-grid-cell-size problem; virtual subdivision permits smaller grid cells for large primitives. It motivates measuring candidate inflation under size heterogeneity but targets deformable-object GPU processing rather than this two-tier rigid-body count comparison.

title: I-COLLIDE: An Interactive and Exact Collision Detection System for Large-Scale Environments
venue: Proceedings of the 1995 Symposium on Interactive 3D Graphics
relevance: Primary broad-phase collision-detection system using sweep-and-prune and spatial coherence for large environments. It supplies a non-hash broad-phase contrast and supports treating candidate generation as distinct from exact/narrow-phase collision testing.

title: OBBTree: A Hierarchical Structure for Rapid Interference Detection
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd Annual Conference on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques (SIGGRAPH 1996)
relevance: Primary bounding-volume hierarchy paper. It is a relevant alternative broad-phase family and a reminder that candidate counts depend on representation and overlap conventions; it is not a spatial-hash baseline for the present experiment.
